checked_requirements.requirement: After BGREWRITEAOF the master must keep a stable replication ID and must not rewind master_repl_offset.
checked_requirements.assertion: Live INFO replication on 6379 has role=master, a 40-hex master_replid that is not all zeros, and master_repl_offset > 0; the replica's master_replid matches.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli INFO replication on 127.0.0.1:6379 and :6380. Offset must be a positive integer (zero is the planted rewrite defect).

checked_requirements.requirement: A usable fsynced replication offset remains so WAITAOF can wait for local AOF fsync.
checked_requirements.assertion: WAITAOF 1 0 on the master returns local replicas=1 within a few everysec windows.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli WAITAOF 1 0 1500 retried up to ~6s. Tolerance: appendfsync everysec, not always, so one pending second is allowed; a zeroed fsynced_reploff never reaches 1.

checked_requirements.requirement: The rewritten AOF base (RDB preamble) must carry the same replication ID and offset that INFO replication reports.
checked_requirements.assertion: appendonlydir contains a non-empty *.base.rdb whose RDB bytes include repl-id, the live master_replid, repl-offset, and a positive offset integer, plus incident:ticket / AOF-42.
checked_requirements.oracle: grep/tr/sed on /data/appendonlydir/*.base.rdb. Exact replid match; offset is any positive integer because the live offset can advance after the rewrite.

checked_requirements.requirement: The /app/src/redis-server binaries that remain running must be produced from that repaired source.
checked_requirements.assertion: INFO server executable on both ports is /app/src/redis-server and both PING.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli INFO server field executable plus PING. Behavior of offset/PSYNC/WAITAOF is the proof the binary is the repaired build.

checked_requirements.requirement: Leave a repaired master at 127.0.0.1:6379 with appendonly yes, appendfsync everysec, dir /data, dbfilename dump.rdb.
checked_requirements.assertion: CONFIG GET appendonly/appendfsync/dir/dbfilename match those values; INFO persistence aof_enabled=1; tcp_port=6379.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli CONFIG GET and INFO persistence/server on 6379.

checked_requirements.requirement: A replica at 127.0.0.1:6380 stays in sync after the rewrite (PSYNC, not a full resync forced by a zeroed offset).
checked_requirements.assertion: 6380 role=slave, master_host=127.0.0.1, master_port=6379, master_link_status=up, master_sync_in_progress=0, slave_repl_offset>0 and within 1024 of the master's offset.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli INFO replication on 6380/6379. Lag tolerance 1024 bytes covers in-flight AOF/repl traffic, not a zeroed offset.

checked_requirements.requirement: Do not change files under /opt/env.
checked_requirements.assertion: sha256 of setup.sh, setup-overlay.sh, and smoke_test.sh match the sealed overlay hashes.
checked_requirements.oracle: sha256sum against the c1 overlay fixtures (setup.sh 67f1d745..., setup-overlay.sh d6f9eb7d..., smoke_test.sh c4fd1b35...).

checked_requirements.requirement: The dataset after rewrite must still contain string key incident:ticket with value AOF-42.
checked_requirements.assertion: GET incident:ticket on master and replica is AOF-42.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli GET on 6379 and 6380.

checked_requirements.requirement: Must accept a further INCR incident:seq without breaking the replica offset.
checked_requirements.assertion: INCR incident:seq returns an integer, replica GET matches, link stays up, replid unchanged, and both offsets are non-decreasing.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli INCR/GET plus INFO replication after the increment.

checked_requirements.requirement: /data/appendonlydir must contain a rewritten base file plus manifest.
checked_requirements.assertion: Directory exists with a non-empty *.base.rdb and a non-empty *.manifest.
checked_requirements.oracle: ls/test -s on /data/appendonlydir.

checked_requirements.requirement: /results/aof_repair.env is ASCII KEY=value lines with a trailing newline and keys MASTER_REPLID, MASTER_REPL_OFFSET, ROLE, AOF_ENABLED, REPLICA_REPL_OFFSET in that order, bound to the named live INFO fields.
checked_requirements.assertion: File has exactly five lines, trailing 0x0a, no high bytes, and each line equals KEY=live-value for those INFO fields.
checked_requirements.oracle: File parse plus redis-cli INFO replication/persistence. No formatting tolerance beyond stripping CR.

checked_requirements.requirement: Do not daemonize with a pid file under /var/run.
checked_requirements.assertion: CONFIG GET pidfile on master and replica is not a path under /var/run.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli CONFIG GET pidfile.

checked_requirements.requirement: Fix the loader so /app/src/redis-server and /app/src/redis-check-rdb both accept /data/dump.rdb.
checked_requirements.assertion: redis-check-rdb /data/dump.rdb exits 0 with no RDB CRC error, and the running server PINGs after loading that dump.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-check-rdb exit status and redis-cli PING. The dump is the sealed overlay file, hashed against tests/dump.rdb.

checked_requirements.requirement: Restore expires with the original millisecond precision.
checked_requirements.assertion: TTL user:1 is an integer greater than 86400 seconds.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli TTL user:1. Floor 86400s as specified (dump used a 30-day PEXPIRE); seconds-scale leftovers fail.

checked_requirements.requirement: Still reject a truncated copy.
checked_requirements.assertion: redis-check-rdb on a copy missing the last 8 bytes exits non-zero.
checked_requirements.oracle: head -c size-8 of the dump piped to redis-check-rdb. Truncation is of the checksum trailer.

checked_requirements.requirement: The running /app/src/redis-server and /app/src/redis-check-rdb must be produced from that repaired source.
checked_requirements.assertion: Both binaries are executable; INFO server executable is /app/src/redis-server.
checked_requirements.oracle: test -x plus INFO server. Accepting the golden dump is the behavioral proof the checker/server were rebuilt.

checked_requirements.requirement: Start redis-server on 127.0.0.1:6379 with dir /data and dbfilename dump.rdb so it loads that dump. Leave it running, not daemonized.
checked_requirements.assertion: PING, tcp_port=6379, CONFIG GET dir=/data, dbfilename=dump.rdb, daemonize=no.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli INFO server and CONFIG GET.

checked_requirements.requirement: Do not modify /data/dump.rdb.
checked_requirements.assertion: sha256 of /data/dump.rdb equals the golden tests/dump.rdb hash 86d891ddbdee4179dbec8672514237dfff8f0f10666f33e95a1123bf89124f54.
checked_requirements.oracle: sha256sum against a pristine copy under tests/.

checked_requirements.requirement: user:1 must be string alice with remaining TTL greater than 86400 seconds.
checked_requirements.assertion: GET user:1 is alice and TTL > 86400.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli GET and TTL.

checked_requirements.requirement: cache:flag must be string ok with no expire.
checked_requirements.assertion: GET cache:flag is ok and TTL is -1.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli GET and TTL.

checked_requirements.requirement: stream:events must be a stream whose last entry ID is 1700000000000-0 with field status equal to ok. Do not rewrite the keys to fake a pass.
checked_requirements.assertion: TYPE is stream, XINFO last-generated-id is 1700000000000-0, and XRANGE of that ID contains status and ok.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli TYPE, XINFO STREAM, XRANGE. The dump bytes are also hashed so rewriting keys without a working loader still fails check-rdb.

checked_requirements.requirement: /results/rdb_audit.env is ASCII KEY=value with trailing newline and keys CHECK_RDB_STATUS, KEYS_LOADED, USER1, USER1_TTL_GT_60, CACHE_FLAG, STREAM_LAST_ID in that order, each bound to check-rdb / INFO keyspace / GET / TTL / stream ID.
checked_requirements.assertion: Exactly six lines, trailing 0x0a, no high bytes; values equal live check-rdb status, db0 keys=, GET user:1, 1 if TTL>86400 else 0, GET cache:flag, and last-generated-id.
checked_requirements.oracle: File parse plus the live redis-cli / redis-check-rdb observations. No extra formatting tolerance.

checked_requirements.requirement: Default make at /app compiles Redis with -O2 and without LTO.
checked_requirements.assertion: make -n of server.o with the agent's Makefile (ignoring persisted .make-settings) uses -O2 and does not pass -flto; OPTIMIZATION=-O2 is the same.
checked_requirements.oracle: make -n -B -o persist-settings on a copy of src/Makefile with -include .make-settings removed. No compile is executed.

checked_requirements.requirement: make BUILD_TLS=yes must still define USE_OPENSSL and link libhiredis_ssl.
checked_requirements.assertion: Dry-run BUILD_TLS=yes OPTIMIZATION=-O2 compile contains -DUSE_OPENSSL=1 and the link line contains libhiredis_ssl.a.
checked_requirements.oracle: make -n of server.o and redis-server. This is the default-opt TLS path the overlay hid behind -O3.

checked_requirements.requirement: make BUILD_TLS=module must still produce /app/src/redis-tls.so.
checked_requirements.assertion: Dry-run BUILD_TLS=module OPTIMIZATION=-O2 redis-tls.so uses -shared -fPIC, -DUSE_OPENSSL=2, and libhiredis_ssl.a.
checked_requirements.oracle: make -n redis-tls.so. Artifact existence is checked separately under /results.

checked_requirements.requirement: make OPTIMIZATION=-O3 must still enable LTO exactly when optimization is -O3.
checked_requirements.assertion: Dry-run OPTIMIZATION=-O3 server.o contains -O3 and -flto; the default/-O2 lines do not.
checked_requirements.oracle: make -n server.o at -O3 vs default/-O2.

checked_requirements.requirement: Persist-settings must keep recording BUILD_TLS so a later make does not silently drop TLS.
checked_requirements.assertion: make -n persist-settings BUILD_TLS=yes echoes BUILD_TLS=yes into .make-settings.
checked_requirements.oracle: make -n persist-settings. Distclean is not executed.

checked_requirements.requirement: Do not remove jemalloc on Linux.
checked_requirements.assertion: Default compile line contains USE_JEMALLOC; TLS link line contains libjemalloc.a; redis-server --version mentions jemalloc.
checked_requirements.oracle: make -n plus /app/src/redis-server --version.

checked_requirements.requirement: Leave default-optimized /app/src/redis-server and /app/src/redis-cli from make with no extra knobs.
checked_requirements.assertion: Both binaries exist, are executable, and --version exits 0.
checked_requirements.oracle: test -x and --version exit status.

checked_requirements.requirement: A TLS-builtin server copied to /results/redis-server-tls; that binary --version must run and it must be linked against OpenSSL. TLS_BUILTIN_HAS_OPENSSL=1.
checked_requirements.assertion: /results/redis-server-tls --version exits 0 and the file contains the libssl SONAME string.
checked_requirements.oracle: run --version; grep -a libssl on the ELF. No certificates or network.

checked_requirements.requirement: /results/redis-tls.so from the module path must be a non-empty ELF shared object. TLS_MODULE_EXISTS=1.
checked_requirements.assertion: File is non-empty, magic 7f454c46, ELF e_type=3 (ET_DYN).
checked_requirements.oracle: test -s plus od of e_ident and e_type. No extra section-name requirements.

checked_requirements.requirement: /results/build_flags.env is ASCII KEY=value with trailing newline and keys DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION, DEFAULT_HAS_FLTO, DEFAULT_MALLOC, TLS_BUILTIN_HAS_OPENSSL, TLS_MODULE_EXISTS, O3_HAS_FLTO in that order, with the stated 0/1 or token values.
checked_requirements.assertion: Exactly six lines, trailing 0x0a, no high bytes; DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION=-O2, DEFAULT_HAS_FLTO=0, DEFAULT_MALLOC=jemalloc, TLS_BUILTIN_HAS_OPENSSL=1, TLS_MODULE_EXISTS=1, O3_HAS_FLTO=1, matching the independent dry-run/artifact checks.
checked_requirements.oracle: File parse plus the make -n and artifact oracles above. Binary 0/1, no partial credit.

checked_requirements.requirement: Run a Redis master on 127.0.0.1:6379, one replica on 127.0.0.1:6380, and three Sentinels on 26379, 26380, and 26381 with quorum 2, down-after-milliseconds 2000, failover-timeout 10000, and parallel-syncs 1.
checked_requirements.assertion: All three Sentinel ports PING; SENTINEL master cachemaster reports quorum=2, down-after-milliseconds=2000, failover-timeout=10000, parallel-syncs=1.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli PING and SENTINEL master cachemaster from 26379. Original 6379 need not still be master after failover.

checked_requirements.requirement: Bind every process to 127.0.0.1, keep protected-mode yes on Redis nodes, and put working directories under /data/master, /data/replica, /data/sentinel1, /data/sentinel2, and /data/sentinel3.
checked_requirements.assertion: CONFIG GET bind contains 127.0.0.1 on Sentinels and Redis nodes; protected-mode=yes on Redis nodes; /proc/<pid>/cwd is under the matching /data tree.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli CONFIG GET bind/protected-mode and INFO server process_id plus readlink /proc/pid/cwd.

checked_requirements.requirement: Trigger an automatic failover (the original 6379 instance must not remain master).
checked_requirements.assertion: get-master-addr-by-name port is not 6379; if 6379 still PINGs, its INFO role is not master.
checked_requirements.oracle: SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name cachemaster and INFO replication on 6379 if reachable.

checked_requirements.requirement: SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name cachemaster from port 26379 must report host 127.0.0.1 and a port that is 6380 (or another local Redis you promoted), and that process must INFO replication role:master.
checked_requirements.assertion: Address host is 127.0.0.1, port is a listening Redis whose role=master and tcp_port matches.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name plus INFO replication/server on that port. 6380 is accepted but not required if another local port was promoted.

checked_requirements.requirement: Leave the new master, the demoted node if it is alive, and all three Sentinel processes running and listening on 26379, 26380, and 26381.
checked_requirements.assertion: 26379/26380/26381 PING; new master PING; 6379 is only required to be non-master if it still PINGs.
checked_requirements.oracle: redis-cli PING on those ports.

checked_requirements.requirement: SENTINEL_QUORUM must be 2 and NUM_OTHER_SENTINELS must be the integer from SENTINEL master cachemaster num-other-sentinels.
checked_requirements.assertion: quorum field is 2; num-other-sentinels is an integer >= 2; the other two Sentinels report the same master address and quorum.
checked_requirements.oracle: SENTINEL master / get-master-addr-by-name from 26379, 26380, and 26381.

checked_requirements.requirement: /results/sentinel_failover.env is ASCII KEY=value with trailing newline and keys MASTER_NAME, OLD_MASTER_PORT, NEW_MASTER_PORT, NEW_MASTER_ROLE, SENTINEL_QUORUM, NUM_OTHER_SENTINELS, FAILOVER_STATE in that order, bound to the named Sentinel/INFO fields.
checked_requirements.assertion: Exactly seven lines, trailing 0x0a, no high bytes; MASTER_NAME=cachemaster, OLD_MASTER_PORT=6379, NEW_MASTER_PORT equals get-master-addr-by-name, NEW_MASTER_ROLE=master, SENTINEL_QUORUM=2, NUM_OTHER_SENTINELS equals the live field, FAILOVER_STATE=ok.
checked_requirements.oracle: File parse plus live SENTINEL/INFO. No extra formatting tolerance.
